thread:
arjun: Heads up — after the 2.3.1 runtime rollout we started seeing a p99 jump on Qwen-14B routes that use the KV prefix cache. Spike aligns with increased KV memory churn. attaching quick repro logs.

maggie: saw that in the dashboard too, p99 went from ~220ms to ~380ms around 02:17 UTC. Is it only Qwen routes?

lia: looks like Mixtral and Mistral routes are fine. Qwen-specific pattern: large number of short-lived prefixes and immediate eviction, which increases kernel rebinds.

arjun: here's the minimal repro snippet I used (run against staging):

```
curl -s -X POST https://staging.redwood/api/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $STAGING" \
  -d '{"model":"qwen-14b","input":"short prompt","cache_prefix":true,"min_tokens":1}'
```

arjun: stack trace / profiler samples show a lot of time in `kernel_router::select_kernel()` and repeated `kv_cache::evict_entry()` ops.

tomas: 2.3.1 changed the kernel-scheduler heuristics so small batch local routing favors single-stream kernels (to reduce occupancy). That interacts badly when KV evictions cause frequent cache misses -> drops back to slower fallback path.

maggie: hypothesis: kernel selector bias + aggressive segment-LRU eviction = churn. Do we have recent memalloc / slab fragmentation stats?

lia: in /var/prof/kvcache we see rising slab free fragmentation on nodes serving qwen-14b: free slabs are non-contiguous so new KV allocations force memcpy and slab swaps.

arjun: experiment idea: enable hybrid precision: keep keys in FP16 but store values in low-bit FP8 with a per-prefix scale factor (prefix-scale cached). That should halve memory and reduce evictions. Any easy toggle?

ops-bot: deploy flag `kv.hybrid_fp8` exists but default=false in 2.3.x. Toggle is per-node.

maggie: try flipping `kv.hybrid_fp8=true` on a single canary rack and run the repro for 10k requests. Also revert kernel-router to pre-2.3 scheduling for that rack.

tomas: quick micro-benchmark on local: hybrid_fp8 reduced resident KV memory by 46% and cut eviction rate by ~3.2x for synthetic short-prefix workload. But we saw a tiny quality delta on float quant artifacts (need to validate on eval prompts).

lia: also watch RoPE scaling — Qwen uses larger RoPE exponents, which lengthens effective key vectors; FP8 quant noise amplifies if we quantize keys naively. Proposed: only quantize values; keep keys FP16 (or BF16) and use a per-head scale table.

arjun: agreed. For immediate mitigation: (1) canary hybrid_fp8=true + kernel-router revert; (2) bump per-node KV slab size and defragmentation window; (3) add a short-term LRU->clock-protect layer to avoid evicting prefixes that were used in last 2s.

maggie: I'll open a rollout PR and plan canary. Tomas / Lia — can you own bench + eval checks? Need a short quality regression run (SQuAD-ish and 1k prompt fuzz).

tomas: on it. I will also add a small metric: `kv.eviction_tailshare_ratio` to detect tail-heavy evictions vs large-span evictions.

lia: logging note: please avoid printing full key vectors in logs — too big. Use hashed key IDs and head-dim histograms.

arjun: thanks. If canary looks good we'll promote and then iterate on a kernel scheduler fix that accounts for KV miss penalty in the decision function.

maggie: thanks everyone :thumbsup: I'll schedule the canary for 03:20 UTC and post back results in this thread.

dev-deploy-bot: canary started on rack-r14 at 03:20 UTC. Flags: kv.hybrid_fp8=true kernel_router.mode=legacy.

maggie: initial canary numbers: p50 stable, p95 down 10%, p99 down 28% vs pre-toggle. Need more runs for quality but looks promising.

arjun: great. follow-up tickets: #INF-832 (kernel-router adaptive penalty), #INF-833 (kv: per-prefix scale + quant-v-only), #INF-834 (slab defrag job).
